planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun.

directions: Sombrero Poco Hot Coral is one of the dwarf Sombrero Poco members of Terra Nova Nurseries' Sombrero coneflower breeding series, selected to stay under about sixteen inches tall while keeping the heavy branching and vivid coral-orange flower color of the larger Sombrero line. Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; its compact scale suits border fronts and containers where taller coneflowers would overwhelm the planting. It blooms heavily from early summer into fall and draws bees and butterflies steadily, with seed heads left standing into winter feeding goldfinches. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun.

directions: Sombrero Adobe Orange is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction in the Sombrero coneflower series, carrying warm, terracotta-toned orange flowers over a dense, well-branched mound. Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun, where it tolerates heat and drought well once established. Like other Sombrero-series coneflowers it flowers heavily from early summer through fall and is a reliable draw for bees and butterflies. Deadhead to extend bloom, or leave some seed heads for winter interest and finches, and divide every few years to keep plants vigorous.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun.

directions: Sombrero Fuchsia Fandango brings a vivid magenta-pink flower color to Terra Nova Nurseries' compact Sombrero coneflower series, held on the same dense, heavily branched habit that distinguishes the line from older, floppier coneflower hybrids. Grow in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; established plants are heat and drought tolerant and need minimal supplemental watering. Continuous bloom from early summer into fall makes it a strong pollinator plant, and clumps benefit from division every three to four years to sustain vigorous flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun.

directions: Sombrero Granada Gold is a golden-yellow-flowered member of Terra Nova Nurseries' Sombrero coneflower series, adding a clear warm-yellow option to a line otherwise dominated by reds, oranges, and pinks. It shares the series' dense, well-branched, compact habit and strong repeat bloom from early summer through fall. Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; once established it handles heat and drought with little care. Divide clumps every few years in spring if flowering begins to decline.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun.

directions: Sombrero Mandarin Mambo carries bright tangerine-orange flowers on the same compact, densely branched plant typical of Terra Nova Nurseries' Sombrero breeding series. Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun, where its vigorous branching produces a heavier flush of bloom than older single-stem coneflower cultivars. It flowers from early summer into fall and is a steady source of nectar and pollen for bees and butterflies. Deadhead to prolong bloom or let seed heads stand for winter interest, and divide congested clumps every few years.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun.

directions: Sombrero Rosada (Spanish for 'rose-colored') is a rose-pink flowered selection in Terra Nova Nurseries' Sombrero coneflower series, bred for the same compact, heavily branched habit and reliable perennial return found throughout the line. Grow in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; plants tolerate heat and drought well once established and rarely need staking. Bloom runs from early summer through fall and attracts bees and butterflies steadily. Divide every three to four years in spring to keep clumps vigorous.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun.

directions: Sombrero Tres Amigos is notable within Terra Nova Nurseries' Sombrero coneflower series for flowers that shift through multiple tones as they age and open at different times on the same plant, giving a multicolor effect on one well-branched, compact clump. Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; it shares the series' heat and drought tolerance and heavy, continuous summer-to-fall bloom. Deadhead to encourage further flowering or leave seed heads for winter birds, and divide congested clumps every few years to renew vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun.

directions: Sombrero Blanco (Spanish for 'white hat') supplies a clean white-flowered option within Terra Nova Nurseries' Sombrero coneflower series, set against the same compact, densely branched habit bred throughout the line. Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; established clumps are heat and drought tolerant and bloom heavily from early summer into fall. It is a reliable pollinator plant for bees and butterflies and benefits from division every few years to maintain strong flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun.

directions: Eye-Catcher Tanager is part of a coneflower breeding line named for its vivid, songbird-bright flower coloring, grown on an upright, well-branched plant sized for a mixed border. Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun; once established it is drought tolerant and flowers continuously from early summer through fall. It draws bees and butterflies steadily through the bloom season, and leaving some seed heads standing into winter provides food for goldfinches. Divide clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun.

directions: Double Scoop Orangeberry belongs to the fully double Double Scoop coneflower line, producing dense, pompom-like orange-toned blooms without a visible central cone, in contrast to the single-rayed form of straight Echinacea purpurea. Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun; the extra petal layers make for a long-lasting, showy cut flower as well as a garden pollinator plant, though the fully double flowers offer less exposed pollen than single-form coneflowers. Established plants are heat and drought tolerant, blooming from early to late summer. Divide clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun.

directions: Double Dipped Rainbow Sherbet is a fully double coneflower carrying multi-toned peachy-pink petals layered densely enough to largely hide the central cone, part of a Double Dipped breeding line bred for this pompom-style bloom form. Grow in well-drained, average soil in full sun; plants bloom from early to late summer and remain heat and drought tolerant once established. Because the flowers are so densely petaled, pollinator access is more limited than on single-form coneflowers, though bees still visit readily. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring.

common_name: Pardon My Lavender II Bee Balm

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: Pardon My Lavender II is an improved sport within Walters Gardens' extremely compact Pardon My bee balm series, selected for better vigor or color consistency over the original Pardon My Lavender while keeping the series' notably strong resistance to powdery mildew. It forms a tidy, dense mound well under knee height, covered in the classic shaggy, tubular lavender flowers that hummingbirds and bees seek out. Plant in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, with generous spacing to maximize airflow and further reduce mildew pressure. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Summit Sweets Ruby is a deep ruby-red flowered member of the large-growing Summit Sweets beardtongue series, joining the earlier Summit Sweets Purple as a back-of-border option with tall, tubular flower spikes from spring through summer. Plant in well-drained soil in full sun; it tolerates heat and drought well once established and benefits from monthly fertilizing to support its substantial size. Removing spent flower stems encourages continued bloom, which draws bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds steadily through the season. Good drainage is essential, since penstemon crowns are prone to rot in wet, heavy soil.

planting.note: Set out container plants after the last frost in well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: UpTick Gold & Bronze is a bicolor member of the vegetatively propagated UpTick tickseed series, pairing golden-yellow petal tips with a bronze-red base around each flower's center for a two-toned look distinct from the solid-colored UpTick Gold bred alongside it. Like its series-mates it is sterile and unusually large-flowered for a Coreopsis, channeling its energy into nonstop bloom from late spring through hard frost rather than seed production, so deadheading is unnecessary. Site it in lean to average, sharply drained soil in full sun, since crowns are prone to winter rot in heavy, wet ground. A light midseason shearing refreshes the compact, mounded habit if plants begin to sprawl in richer soil.
